newsitem.title: BAHAMAS: Authorities investigate Cunard ship fire.
newsitem.headline: Authorities investigate Cunard ship fire.

text.p: Hundreds of passengers waited on board the Cunard cruise ship Vistafjord on Monday as it remained docked in Freeport, Bahamas, while authorities investigated a weekend fire that left one crewman dead.

Bahamas Police Superintendent Archie Ferguson identified the dead man as Stephen Moller, a German waiter who was found in a cabin in "an unconscious state" after the fire broke out on Sunday. He said Moller, who was in his 20s, had died at Rand Memorial Hospital in Freeport.

The fire broke out in a linen locker aboard the ship within hours of its Saturday evening departure from Fort Lauderdale on a trans-Atlantic cruise to Funchal on the Portuguese island of Madeira. The ship, which carried 991 passengers and crew, radioed for help within hours of leaving Florida and was diverted to Freeport.
Freeport harbor officials said most of the passengers remained on board and were comfortable, adding that the ship might be able to continue the cruise if the damage could be repaired.
"It's a good thing it happened early while it was fairly close to land," David Johnson, executive vice president of the Grand Bahama Tourism Board, said.

Hundreds of passengers were mustered on deck at emergency stations and other ships in the area were diverted to the scene in case evacuation was needed, but the pre-dawn fire did not spread beyond the ship's laundry, officials said.

A spokesman for New York-based Cunard Line Ltd., owner of the 627-foot (190-metre) Bahamian-registered vessel, said another crew member suffered a broken ankle and a passenger broke an arm. Cunard is a subsidiary of the Norwegian shipbuilding group Kvaerner ASA.

Cunard said smoke had spread to cabins and passageways but fire damage was contained to the linen locker area on the ship's third deck toward the stern. The fire was put out shortly after the Vistafjord arrived in Freeport.
